desc:
A PrestaShop store audit and fix list shows what is slowing, weakening or confusing your shop, ranked by impact and effort. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your version, modules, security, speed and checkout, then hands you a plain written report.

## What is a PrestaShop store audit?

A PrestaShop audit is a structured review of a live shop that ends in a written, ranked list of problems and fixes. It looks at the same things a shopper meets and the same things a developer would inspect: the installed version, the module list, back office security settings, page speed, mobile display, product pages, the cart and the checkout.

The goal is not a pile of warnings. The goal is a short answer to the question "what should I fix first?" so you can spend your time and budget on the changes that matter.

## Why PrestaShop shops drift out of shape

PrestaShop is flexible, and that flexibility is also how shops get messy. Over time a store collects modules from different authors, theme overrides, old test settings and half-finished experiments. Each one is harmless alone. Together they can slow pages down, create conflicts between modules and leave admin settings that should have been closed.

Nobody notices until something breaks, such as a payment step that fails on phones or a category page that takes too long to open. An audit finds these weak spots before a customer does.

## How an audit improves results

An audit improves results by removing friction you cannot see from the inside. You know your own shop too well to spot a confusing button or a slow product page. A fresh review reveals where shoppers may hesitate, where the shop wastes loading time, and where a security setting leaves the back office more exposed than it should be.

Ranking matters as much as finding. A list of fifty issues with no order leads to nothing getting done. When every finding carries an impact level and an effort level, you can pick the quick wins first and plan the larger jobs later. Fewer broken steps in the buying path means fewer lost orders, and a faster, safer shop is easier to run.

## What a good PrestaShop audit includes

- The PrestaShop version in use, and whether it is behind the current release.
- The full module list, with notes on overlap, abandoned modules and conflicts.
- Back office security settings, admin folder and account hygiene.
- A speed check of the home page, a category page and a product page, on mobile and desktop.
- A shopper walkthrough from product page to cart to checkout.
- Mobile display checks on real screen sizes.
- Search basics such as titles, descriptions and duplicate pages.
- Tracking and analytics checks, so you know your numbers can be trusted.
- Screenshots next to every finding.
- Plain fix steps that you or a developer can follow.

## How we run your audit

We start with the access you give us as a staff or collaborator user, and we work only in your own shop. We never need a password. First we record the version, the modules and the key settings. Then we test the store as a shopper, on a phone and on a computer, and note each point of friction.

Next we write the report. Every finding has a title, a screenshot, an explanation in everyday words, the likely impact, the effort to fix it and the steps to do so. The Basic package covers the essentials and a ranked list of the main issues. Standard adds the shopper walkthrough, a module review and a longer list of findings. Premium adds search and tracking checks, a call to go through the report together and a month-long action plan.

We report and recommend. If you want the fixes made, that is a separate piece of work we can quote from your list.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us which pages bring the most visitors and orders, so we test those first.
- Mention any recent changes, such as a new module or an upgrade.
- Share known complaints from customers or staff.
- Work through the list in ranked order, starting with high impact and low effort.
- Keep a copy of the report so you can compare after the fixes.

**Avoid:**
- Fixing things on the live shop before you have a backup.
- Updating every module at once without testing each one.
- Treating a low-scoring speed test as the only measure of a healthy store.
- Ignoring security notes because the shop seems to work fine.
- Deleting modules from the list without checking what depends on them.

## Who this is for

This audit suits owners who inherited a PrestaShop store from an earlier developer and do not know what is inside it. It suits sellers whose sales have stalled and who want an outside view before spending on new features. It also suits teams preparing for an upgrade or a redesign who need to know the starting condition.

## How to get started

Send us your shop address and a short note about your main concerns. Add staff or collaborator access to the back office so we can review the settings without touching your data. We reply with a short checklist, confirm the package and deliver the written report. Add-ons such as an extra call, a module cost review or a task board version of the list are available if you want them.
